extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians and computational-proof researchers implementing/verifying the Kepler-conjecture LP+interval-arithmetic approach
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and evaluative criteria for constructing linear-program relaxations of the nonlinear optimization over decomposition stars in the Kepler conjecture proof, and for branch-and-bound case-splitting, error control, and elimination of pathological aggregates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of a relaxation (interpretation I)
rubrics_metrics.description: The interpretation I of an LP is a relaxation of the nonlinear program (NLP) if (1) P = |I|, (2) the constraints A x ≤ b are satisfied under I, and (3) f(p) ≤ c · xI(p) for all p ∈ |I|.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this three-part test to certify that an LP provides a valid upper bound on the nonlinear objective on domain P; then any feasible LP solution yields a feasible point for the LP and any LP upper bound M is an upper bound for f on |I| (Lemma 12.2).

rubrics_metrics.name: LP-derived inequalities
rubrics_metrics.description: An inequality e · x ≤ b' is said to be LP-derived (with respect to A x ≤ b) if max(e·x : A x ≤ b) ≤ b'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To show a nonlinear inequality holds under an interpretation, solve the LP max(e·x : A x ≤ b); if the maximum ≤ b' then e·x ≤ b' is satisfied under the interpretation (Remark 12.4). These LP-derived inequalities may be added to the LPs as constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence and coverage of finite LP sequence (Theorem 12.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each tame plane graph G (except listed exceptions) there exists a finite sequence of linear programs such that (1) every LP has an admissible solution and its solution is strictly less than 8 pt; (2) for every LP there is an interpretation I that is a relaxation of the NLP where |I| ⊂ DS(G); (3) the union of the |I| over the sequence equals DS(G).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Constructive requirement: generate and solve a finite set of LPs by computer so their interpretations (relaxations) together exhaust the decomposition-star space DS(G) and each gives a score bound < 8 pt. The paper estimates ≈105 LPs for the construction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indexing, variables, and variable bounds for the basic LP
rubrics_metrics.description: Use indexing sets VERTEX, FACE, ANGLE, DIRECTED, TRIANGLES, UNDIRECTED and introduce variables α{ANGLE}, σ{FACE}, y{VERTEX}, τ{FACE}, e{UNDIRECTED}, sol{FACE} with bounds such as 0 ≤ y[v] ≤ 2t0, 0 ≤ e[v,w] ≤ 2t0, 0 ≤ α[v,F] ≤ 2π, 0 ≤ sol[F] ≤ 4π.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Declare variables AMPL-style and include explicit geometric bounds arising from definitions and geometry. Many additional inequalities (from interval arithmetic) tie these variables together for specific face lengths.

rubrics_metrics.name: Linear geometric relations to include
rubrics_metrics.description: Include linear relations suggested by geometry: τ[F] = sol[F] ζpt − σ[F], sum_{v∈F} α[v,F] = 2π, sol[F] = sum_{v∈F} α[v,F] − (len(F)−2)π, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These equalities/relations are mandatory linear constraints in LPs to model dihedral/solid-angle/score relationships (Section 12.3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of interval-arithmetic verified nonlinear inequalities
rubrics_metrics.description: Many nonlinear inequalities entering the interpretation are verified by interval arithmetic on computer and are listed externally (e.g., [Hal05]); these nonlinear inequalities are used to justify that A xI ≤ b under interpretation I.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat interval-arithmetic verifications as certificates that certain nonlinear relations hold pointwise on |I|; either include LP-derived linear consequences or validate by interval checks as part of interpretation verification (Remark 12.3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Floating-point error control and rigorous checking
rubrics_metrics.description: Floating-point LP results (e.g., from CPLEX) must be checked rigorously: obtain an approximate dual z with z ≥ 0 and zA ≥ c − ε, with ε small (e.g., < 10−8); if the numerical bound p pt + z·b < 7.9999 pt and ε < 10−8 then conclude σ(D) < 8 pt (Section 12.4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the given perturbation analysis: replace negative entries of z by 0, control factor (1+ε) denominators, and account additively for ε(p pt + 2πN). Verify error thresholds (examples: 7.9999 pt target, ε < 1e-8) to deduce strict <8 pt bounds. Double-check LPs with interval arithmetic when possible (footnote).

rubrics_metrics.name: Branching rules for triangular faces
rubrics_metrics.description: When a single LP is insufficient, divide triangular faces (v1,v2,v3) into two subcases according to e[v1,v2] + e[v2,v3] + e[v3,v1] ≤ 6.25 or ≥ 6.25 (Section 13.1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this binary split on triangle perimeter to create sub-LPs as part of branch-and-bound; combine across r1 triangles and r2 quadrilaterals to obtain up to 2^{r1+2r2} cases in worst case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quadrilateral face case-splitting
rubrics_metrics.description: Quadrilateral faces are split into four subcases: two flat-quarters, two flat-quarters with diagonal in other direction, four upright quarters (quartered octahedron), and the mixed case (Section 13.1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply these geometric classifications to break quadrilateral standard regions into exhaustive subcases for LP branching; no further comment required when used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptional-face constraints (LP additions)
rubrics_metrics.description: For special aggregates/exceptional faces add linear inequalities such as τ[F] > t_k and σ[F] < pt + s_k (examples: τ[F] > t8 and σ[F] < pt + s8 for hexagons) to the LP when an aggregate exists (Sections 13.2–13.4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a potential aggregate/exceptional face is present, include these extra constraints in LPs; rerun LPs for all tame graphs with such constraints and check resulting bounds <8 pt to eliminate cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: LP-derived numeric bounds for pentagonal cases (example thresholds)
rubrics_metrics.description: In pentagonal-hull cases LP-derived inequalities include y[vi] ≤ 2.168, α[vi,F] ≤ 2.89, σ[F] > −0.2345, τ[F] < 0.644; branch-and-bound can improve τ[F] < 0.6079; perimeter bounds |vi−vi+1| ≤ 11.407 and local perimeter sums |v1−v2|+|v2−v3| < 4.804 are also LP-derived (Section 13.4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate these explicit numeric bounds into LPs for the pentagonal/hull subcase; use contradictions between derived lower/upper bounds (e.g., τR(D) > 0.6079 vs τ[F] < 0.6079) to eliminate cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elimination of aggregates / uniqueness of region correspondence
rubrics_metrics.description: For contravening decomposition stars, every face of G must correspond to exactly one standard region of D and no standard region has enclosed vertices from U(D); thus aggregates shown in earlier figures do not occur (Theorem 13.1, Lemma 13.4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use LPs and interval-verified inequalities to show these aggregate cases yield LP bounds <8 pt and thus can be eliminated from consideration; ensure in models that faces correspond one-to-one with standard regions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of upright-diagonal contexts and loop bounds (Lemma 14.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Allowed contexts (n,k) for an upright-diagonal loop are enumerated by standard region type (quad/pent/hex/hept/oct) with associated upper bounds σ and lower bounds τ for σR(D) and τR(D) respectively (table in Lemma 14.1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a loop is present, enforce the associated numeric σ/τ bounds for that context in LPs; these constants serve as constraints to reduce feasible space and produce LP bounds under 8 pt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and consequences of 3-crowded / 3-unconfined / 4-crowded upright diagonals
rubrics_metrics.description: An upright diagonal (not a loop) with context (4,1) is 3-crowded if its three quarters lie in same half-space separated by a plane, otherwise 3-unconfined; context (5,1) is 4-crowded. A contravening decomposition star contains at most one upright diagonal that is 3-crowded or 4-crowded (Definition 14.2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classify upright diagonals accordingly and apply the specialized bounds and elimination lemmas; presence of 3-crowded or 4-crowded diagonals triggers additional LP constraints/branching.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numeric bounds for crowded upright diagonals (Lemma 14.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: If R contains an upright diagonal that is 4-crowded then σR(D) < −0.25 and τR(D) > 0.4. If R contains a 3-crowded upright diagonal then σR(D) < −0.4339 and τR(D) > 0.5606.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Add these strict numeric inequalities to LPs when such configurations arise; they are strong enough to eliminate cases (Lemma 14.4 and following).

rubrics_metrics.name: Erasure of upright diagonals with penalty πR
rubrics_metrics.description: An upright diagonal {0,v} can be erased with penalty πR if σR(D) ≤ σR'(D') + πR (or with any chosen upper-bounds fR(D) replacing σR(D)), where D' is the star with v removed and R' the corresponding subregion (Section 14.4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use erasure-with-penalty to simplify configurations in LPs: removing an upright diagonal is permissible provided you add its penalty to the score-bound. Penalties are computed in unabridged proof and are often integer combinations of ξΓ = 0.01561, ξV = 0.003521, and 0.008.

rubrics_metrics.name: Penalties and specific erasure facts (Lemma 14.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: If upright diagonal is 3-unconfined it can be erased with penalty 0.008; if 3-unconfined and it masks a flat quarter it can be erased with penalty 0; if a flat quarter is masked then its diagonal ≥ 2.6 and if diagonal ≤ 2.7 then central vertex height ≥ 2.2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply these concrete numerical erasure rules to remove diagonals in LP cases and adjust score bounds by the specified penalties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pentagon/hexagon/heptagon/octagon face refinements and penalties
rubrics_metrics.description: Refinement diagrams enumerate possible quarter/anchor arrangements for pentagons, hexagons, heptagons, octagons; many cases carry explicit penalties (examples: hexagonal first two top-row figures have penalties 2(0.008) and 0.008; bottom row have penalties 3ξΓ etc.) (Section 14.5–14.6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When breaking faces into subcases, consult the refinement lists and attach the given penalties to erased loops or erased upright diagonals; these penalties are included in LP bounds to account for simplifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special numeric constants for hept/oct case-analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Define Z(3,1)=0.00005 and D(3,1)=0.06585; these enter inequalities used in one- and two-flat-quarter analyses for heptagons/octagons (Section 14.6.1–14.6.2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Z(3,1) as a small subtraction in σ upper bounds for masked flat quarters and D(3,1) as small subtractions in τ lower bounds when combining subregions; include these constants when applying the stated combinatorial inequalities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Branching upright diagonals by height and anchor thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: Break upright-diagonal cases by: (1) height |v| ≤ 2.696; (2) |v| ≥ 2.696 and some anchor w satisfies |w| ≥ 2.45 or |v−w| ≥ 2.45 (separate case per anchor); (3) |v| ≥ 2.696 and every anchor satisfies |w| ≤ 2.45 and |v−w| ≤ 2.45 (Section 14.7).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these numeric thresholds to partition configuration space for LP-specific inequalities; incorporate inequalities tailored to these domains to tighten LP bounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Erasure/score inequalities for upright quarters (compression and Voronoi types)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an upright quarter Q has compression type and diagonal height ≥ 2.696 then σ(Q) < s-vor0(Q) (erased without penalty). If Q is Voronoi type and anchors satisfy |w| ≤ 2.45 and |v−w| ≤ 2.45 then Q can be erased (calc references). Generally σ(Q) < s-vor0(Q) + 0.003521 may hold (Sections 14.7).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classify upright quarters as compression or Voronoi type and apply the corresponding erasure inequality; when erasing, replace contribution of Q by s-vor0(Q) and possible small additive penalty (0.003521) if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Branching and criteria for flat quarters (height/diagonal threshold)
rubrics_metrics.description: If all three corners of a flat quarter have heights ≤ 2.14 and diagonal < 2.77 then circumradius < √2 and the flat quarter has compression type; Lemma 14.14: either σ(Q)=Γ(Q), or diagonal ≤ 2.7 and η(y4,y5,y6) ≥ √2 and σ(Q) ≤ s-vor0(Q), or diagonal ≥ 2.7 and σ(Q) ≤ s-vor0(Q).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these thresholds (2.14, 2.77, 2.7) to branch cases for flat quarters; apply the listed three-way conclusion to decide whether to use Γ(Q) score, s-vor0 bounds, or treat as compression type in LPs.
